newsitem.title: USA: NBA-GUGLIOTTA'S 32 POINTS HELP MINESOTA PAST BOSTON.
newsitem.headline: NBA-GUGLIOTTA'S 32 POINTS HELP MINESOTA PAST BOSTON.

text.p: Tom Gugliotta scored 32 points, grabbed a season-high 19 rebounds and had seven assists as the Minnesota Timberwolves beat the Boston Celtics 94-84 on Friday.

Kevin Garnett scored 16 points and Cherokee Parks added 14 for the Timberwolves. Garnett recorded a career-high eight rejections for Minnesota, which leads the league in that statistic. The Timberwolves held an opponent under 100 points for the first time in 10 road games.
In Chicago, Michael Jordan scored 22 points and Dennis Rodman grabbed 22 rebounds as the Chicago Bulls cruised to their eighth straight home win, routing the Orlando Magic, 110-89.
Toni Kukoc scored 18 points and Scottie Pippen added 16 for Chicago, which improved to 15-1 at home.
"I think Dennis wanted to come and play well tonight," said Jordan. "He was very aggressive offensively and defensively. He really set the tone for us."
In Denver, Carl Herrera nailed a jumper with 2.5 remaining to break a tie and give the shorthanded San Antonio Spurs their third straight victory, 93-91 over the Denver Nuggets.
Vernon Maxwell scored 24 points and Will Perdue and Monty Williams added 12 apiece for the Spurs.
LaPhonso Ellis scored a career-high 30 points, with 15 coming in Denver's 32-point third quarter.
At Indiana, Reggie Miller scored 33 points, including a season-high seven three-pointers, as the Indiana Pacers snapped a three-game losing streak with a 117-104 victory over the Phoenix Suns.
Derrick McKey added 17 points, Jalen Rose had 12 and Dale Davis contributed 10 points and nine rebounds for Indiana.
"We played well after the first quarter," McKey said. "We were a little sluggish and tentative, but we put it together and held our composure ad got the breaks and won."

At New Jersey, Christian Laettner had 24 points and 11 rebounds and Mookie Blaylock added 22 points and 10 boards as the Atlanta Hawks defeated the struggling New Jersey Nets for the 10th straight time, 95-85.
Dikembe Mutombo had 21 points, 12 rebounds and four blocked shots.
Kendall Gill had 28 points, nine rebounds and five assists for the Nets, who have lost three straight and five of their last seven games.
In Vancouver, Gary Payton had 29 points and 10 assists and Shawn Kemp added 19 points and 12 rebounds as the Seattle SuperSonics cruised to a 108-94 victory over the Vancouver Grizzlies.
Detlef Schrempf had 18 points and nine assists for Seattle, which has won seven of its last nine games.
Anthony Peeler scored 24 points and rookie Shareef Abdur-Rahim added 19 for the Grizzlies, who suffered their fourth straight loss.

At Golden State, Latrell Sprewell scored four of his 39 points in overtime and Chris Mullin posted a triple-double as the Golden State Warriors won for the fourth time in five games, 122-114 over the Philadelphia 76ers.
Mullin had 19 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists, although he was held to just two points in the second half.
Joe Smith scored 28 points for Golden State.

In Los Angeles, Elden Campbell -- starting in place of the injured Shaquille O'Neal -- had 22 points and a season-high 15 rebounds and rookie Kobe Bryant scored 21 points as the Los Angeles Lakers beat the Sacramento Kings, 100-93.
Byron Scott added 15 points and Eddie Jones and Travis Knight each had 12 for Los Angeles.
